items.title: Gravitational Wave Detection via Massive-Particle Interferometry
items.authors: Alireza Maleki
items.abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations provide a powerful means of testing general relativity and exploring the physics of black holes and the early universe, motivating the development of complementary detection techniques. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a GW detector based on massive-particle interferometry, in which the signal is encoded in the relative phase accumulated by a quantum particle traversing a closed-loop trajectory and a reference path. We derive the frequency-dependent GW-induced phase response and examine the parameters on which it depends. items.title: Detection of GRB 261010A with GRID-11B
items.authors: Chenyu Wang, Longhao Li, Xiaofan Pan, Hua Feng, Ming Zeng, Zihan Yu
items.abstract: We report GRID-11B observations of the main emission episode of GRB 261010A. We measure $T_{90}=5.68^{+1.04}_{-0.32}$ s and a minimum variability timescale of $51.6^{+10.5}_{-9.8}$ ms. Its spectrum is described by a cutoff power law with $E_{\rm p}=1089^{+171}_{-80}$ keV. At both candidate host redshifts ($z=0.070$ and $0.785$), the low $\varepsilon$ values and their positions relative to the Amati relation suggest Type-I-like properties. These properties, despite the long duration, resemble those of GRB 211211A and motivate investigation of a possible compact-object merger origin.

items.title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
items.authors: Emiel Claasen, Mehregan Doroudiani, Claude Duhr, Axel Kleinschmidt, Franca Lippert, Oliver Schlotterer, Yoann Sohnle
items.abstract: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples.

items.title: Lost in the Signal Model: Confusion Between Deterministic and Stochastic Gravitational Wave Signals in Pulsar Timing Array Data
items.authors: Caitlin A. Witt, Nihan S. Pol
items.abstract: With growing evidence for the presence of a gravitational wave background (GWB) in pulsar timing array (PTA) data, it is imperative to understand how this signal will act as a foreground for other GW signals, particularly those from individual supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs), which are predicted to be detected in the next decade. For PTAs, since these two types of signals are long-timescale persistent signals, a signal from an SMBHB system may already be present in the latest PTA datasets. items.title: Blazars through the eyes of REDSoX and GOSoX
items.authors: Sara Capecchiacci, Ioannis Liodakis, Herman L. Marshall, Swati Ravi, Haocheng Zhang
items.abstract: Blazar polarimetric properties provide key constraints on the physical conditions within relativistic jets, offering insights into particle acceleration mechanisms, high-energy radiation processes, and jet composition. The Rocket Experiment Demonstration of a Soft X-ray Polarimeter (REDSoX) will serve as a precursor to the Globe Orbiting Soft X-ray Polarimeter (GOSoX), a state-of-the-art polarimeter designed for observations in the soft X-ray range (0.2-0.4 keV), with a planned launch for 2030. REDSoX and GOSoX will be the first (and currently only) X-ray polarimeters capable of performing observations below 1 keV, opening a new observational window into high-energy polarimetry. items.title: A matrix model of an M5--brane on a plane--wave background
items.authors: Carmine Montella
items.abstract: We construct the maximally supersymmetric deformation of the recently proposed $\mathcal{A}_6$ matrix model on a plane--wave background. We derive the same theory independently, by reducing the light--cone M5--brane on a five--sphere in this background to its lowest harmonics, including the dynamics of its chiral two--form and of its fermions. items.title: Agent-guided construction of Feynman integral bases
items.authors: Pau Petit Rosas, William J. Torres Bobadilla
items.abstract: Finding bases of Feynman integrals whose differential equations are suitable for phenomenology is a remarkably verifiable task. We exploit this to design two \emph{skills} with which Claude Opus~5.5 produces novel results autonomously, working for several days. For a two-loop five-point family (with two masses and 18 elliptic sectors) and a two-loop superfamily for the radiative jet function with a K3 sector, the agent finds bases whose differential equations are free of poles in the dimensional regulator $\varepsilon$ and at most quadratic in it, and takes the jet-function one to $\varepsilon$-factorized form.

items.title: The cosmological lithium problem and how decaying relics still solve it
items.authors: Maksym Ovchynnikov
items.abstract: Lithium-7 in old stars is about three times below the prediction of standard big-bang nucleosynthesis, and deuterium lies slightly above it. Precise measurements of deuterium, helium-4, and the effective number of neutrino species now disfavor most previously proposed particle solutions. We find that relics that decay or evaporate with lifetimes of a few hours, mostly into electron antineutrinos of about a hundred MeV and into electrons or photons, still lower lithium-7 while respecting these measurements. items.title: Moment bounds and UV reconstruction from curved positivity cones
items.authors: Fu-Ming Chang, Shi-Lin Wan, Shuang-Yong Zhou
items.abstract: The fundamental principles of the S-matrix impose positivity bounds on the Wilson coefficients of EFTs, including the SMEFT. These bounds form convex cones that often have curved boundaries when there are degeneracies among the irreducible two-particle low-energy states. Numerical approximations have previously been used to evaluate these curved cones. We develop a moment-based framework to analytically carve out these cones, particularly those associated with anomalous quartic gauge couplings in the SMEFT. The framework also allows us to reverse engineer UV models from the curved boundaries of the positivity cones.

items.authors: Felix M. Haehl, Moshe Rozali

At the free-fermion radius, the spin-zero spectrum of the $\mathbb Z_2^4$-invariant sector is exactly degenerate at integer energies. items.title: From Binary Wind to Radio Burst: Dispersion-Measure Evolution after Accretion-induced Collapse
items.authors: Smadar Naoz, Victoria M. Kaspi
items.abstract: Secular changes in the dispersion measures (DMs) of repeating fast radio bursts probe the source-local plasma. Such DM time variability has been interpreted with spherical, single-density-profile models. items.title: Dijet production in $e^+e^-$ collisions at NNLO+PS accuracy
items.authors: Florian K\"onig, Marius Wiesemann, Giulia Zanderighi
items.abstract: We present the first complete Monte Carlo event generator with next-to-next-to-leading order QCD accuracy for lepton collisions. The approach is based on a new formulation of the MiNNLO formalism and is applied to dijet production. Starting from the resummation of the three-jet resolution variable $y_3$, we present the corresponding MiNNLO master formula and implement it within the Powheg framework. We discuss phenomenological results relevant for LEP and future electron-positron colliders.

items.title: NGC 1300: A rich reservoir of ultraluminous X-ray sources
items.authors: Sinan Allak, Faruk Soydugan, Andrea Santangelo, Wei Yu, Santina Piraino, Daniel Kulinsky
items.abstract: We present the first systematic multi-epoch study of the X-ray source population of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 1300, using 12 archival Chandra observations spanning more than 15 years and archival Swift/XRT monitoring. Within the optical extent of the galaxy, we identify 42 X-ray sources, including six ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) and 13 ULX candidates. The candidates have measured luminosities below $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$, but their upper uncertainty bounds reach or exceed this threshold in at least one epoch. items.abstract: We present a study of the screening masses of spin-$3/2$ baryons within a symmetry preserving contact interaction framework. Extending previous finite-temperature investigations of light baryons, we analyze 16 systems composed of $u$, $s$, $c$, and $b$ quarks, including light, heavy-light, and fully-heavy configurations with both positive and negative parity states. items.title: SciPIC-lite: A flexible Halo Occupation Distribution pipeline aimed at clustering observables
items.authors: Gabriele Parimbelli, Martin Crocce, Giosu\`e Gambardella, Alexander Eggemeier, Pablo Fosalba, Elizabeth J. Gonzalez, Sujatha Ramakrishnan, Isaac Tutusaus, Zahra Baghkhani, Jorge Carretero, Francisco Castander, Andrea Pezzotta, Pau Tallada-Cresp\'i
items.abstract: The Halo Occupation Distribution (HOD) framework provides a flexible approach to modelling the galaxy--halo connection in cosmological simulations, encoding the statistical relationship between galaxies and their host dark matter haloes. We present SciPIC-lite, a new public Python library for fast, flexible, and user-friendly HOD modelling, designed to populate dark matter haloes extracted from cosmological simulations with galaxies and to provide a comprehensive suite of tools for their subsequent analysis. items.authors: Yury Kolomensky, Michael MacKenzie, Ryan Plestid, Matthew Stortini, Ajla Trumic
items.abstract: Radiative muon capture (RMC) is an important background in searches for the neutrinoless conversion of a muon into an electron in the field of a nucleus, and in particular in searches for the lepton flavor and lepton number violating process of muon-to-positron conversion. The high-energy tail of the RMC photon spectrum remains theoretically understudied, leading to large uncertainties in background predictions for upcoming muon-conversion experiments. In this work, we revisit previously published RMC data to investigate improved modeling of the high-energy tail. items.title: Kinetic Sunyaev Zel'dovich Velocity Reconstruction Using Vision Transformers
items.authors: Sophie Coulombe, Matthew C. Johnson
items.abstract: Kinetic Sunyaev Zel'dovich (kSZ) velocity reconstruction uses correlations between maps of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and a tracer of large scale structure (LSS) to infer the large-scale peculiar velocity field. Standard approaches to kSZ velocity reconstruction use quadratic estimators that are Fisher optimal for purely Gaussian fields. Here, we develop a pipeline for kSZ velocity reconstruction based on Vision Transformers (ViT) and show that this approach can improve the fidelity of velocity reconstruction. items.authors: Irene Corral Lorences, Zhen Liu, Giuliano Panico, Andrea Wulzer
items.abstract: A proper quantum description of colliding beams reveals the spacetime structure of collision processes, going beyond the conventional picture of classical point-like particles undergoing short-distance scattering. This familiar picture emerges as an approximation in the classical beam limit and under specific conditions. items.authors: Benjamin Luke, Sudip Shiwakoti, Shayan Nadeem, Ronald Morgan, Walter Wilcox
items.abstract: Estimating the trace of the inverse of a large quark matrix is a longstanding problem in lattice QCD. The standard approach is Hutchinson's method, which uses random noise vectors to estimate the trace to a desired statistical tolerance. Each noise vector $b$ requires solving a system of linear equations $Ax = b$. In this work, we introduce a new class of Krylov solvers for this task, called Twin methods. items.authors: James R. Cheshire, Sean T. Bruton, Charuhas W. Shiveshwarkar

As statistical errors shrink with growing galaxy samples, systematic rather than statistical uncertainties come to dominate the cosmological error budget. items.authors: Daniel Mendoza-Fredes, Craig O. Heinke, Matthew Lang, Asma Hattawi
items.abstract: The X-ray source X10 in the globular cluster 47 Tuc has been identified as a cataclysmic variable (CV). With a suggested 4.7 hour periodicity, and a soft X-ray spectrum, it appears to be an unusually X-ray luminous ($L_X=2.2\times10^{32}$ erg s$^{-1}$) polar CV. We use 286 ks of Chandra X-ray Observatory observations of 47 Tuc to study the X-ray timing behavior of 47 Tuc X10. X10 shows clear pulsations in the data, with occasional phase shifts. items.authors: Yuma Furuta, Yuya Kusuki, Toshiki Onagi, Yin Tang
items.abstract: Symmetry constrains how independently energy and charge can pass through a conformal interface. items.authors: Jiaxing Zhao, Shuzhe Shi, Pengfei Zhuang

items.authors: Yugo Abe, Takeo Inami, Keisuke Izumi, Shinsuke Kawai

items.authors: Manqi Fu, Shuying Zhou, Hengxiao Guo, Zhi-Xiang Zhang, Marcin Marculewicz, Mouyuan Sun
items.abstract: Recent continuum reverberation-mapping measurements of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) indicate that the inter-band time lags are significantly larger than those predicted by the light travel times across the standard thin model. In addition, the observed $u$-band excess suggests the presence of diffuse continuum (DC) radiation originating in the broad-line region (BLR). Spectroscopically, the Balmer and Paschen jumps in DC emission are unique indicators to quantify the contributions of the BLR to the observed continuum. items.authors: Hao Wang, Gen Ye, Yun-Song Piao
items.abstract: Early dark energy is commonly characterized by the amplitude and location of its primary energy-injection peak. We construct a simple phenomenological framework in which distinct regions of a multiscale scalar potential govern the dynamics at different field scales. items.authors: Bhaskar Arya, Soumak Maitra, Shadab Alam
items.abstract: The Lyman-$\alpha$ forest probes matter structure at $z\gtrsim2$, constraining baryon acoustic oscillations, neutrino masses, and dark matter properties. Interpreting current and upcoming spectroscopic surveys requires mock catalogues spanning Gpc-scale volumes while capturing small-scale intergalactic medium physics. This combination of high resolution and large volume is prohibitively expensive for hydrodynamical simulations. items.authors: Keunsu Cheon, Sin Kyu Kang, Jungjai Lee

items.abstract: Global analysis of Galactic compact binaries (GCBs) for space-based gravitational-wave detectors is computationally demanding in the high-frequency region (above $\sim$10 mHz), where resolvable signals are sparse but frequency samples are numerous. items.authors: I. Jack, D. R. T. Jones
items.abstract: We consider the $\beta$-functions for both scalar, and supersymmetric chiral scalar, field theories with a general $n$th-order self-interaction, in their critical dimensions, which are in general non-integer. items.authors: Mohamed Belfkir, Ayoub Hmissou, Larbi Rahili

items.authors: L. Nicotera, T. Sprenger, O. Wucknitz, L. G. Spitler, F. Eppel, P. Limaye
items.abstract: Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) are bright, ms-duration, extragalactic radio transients. Propagation through inhomogeneities in the ionised medium produces scintillation, observed as frequency-dependent intensity variations in their spectra, with bright patches, called scintles. The characteristic scintillation bandwidth probes scattering material along the line of sight. Measuring this scale can be challenging when the observing bandwidth of the burst spectra contains a few scintles. items.abstract: We study the holonomic $D$-module whose solutions are generic-mass banana Feynman integrals with complex propagator powers and spacetime dimension. We call this the banana $D$-module. items.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a future space-based gravitational wave (GW) observatory. items.authors: David Dickson, Pablo Marchant, Jon Sundqvist, Mattias Fabry
items.abstract: Mass transfer is a highly dynamical 3D process that spans evolutionary timescales in binary stars. It is key to the production of gravitational waves through formation of binary black holes and other double compact objects. We integrate global 3D hydrodynamics into stellar evolutionary modeling to resolve mass transfer across nuclear timescales. We employ the shellular approximation in the stellar evolution code MESA to map a 3D spatial structure by equipotential shells in the Roche geometry to maintain hydrostatic equilibrium across tidally-distorted surfaces. items.authors: Yizhan Zhang, Suoqing Ji, Guiyun Liang, Shuinai Zhang, Zhijie Qu
items.abstract: Cold-hot interfaces are ubiquitous in the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM), galactic winds, and the Galactic Center (GC), yet their microscopic contact regions are difficult to observe. Charge exchange (CX), in which a highly ionized metal ion captures an electron from a neutral donor and emits soft X-ray lines, directly probes these interfaces. We develop a subgrid CX model coupled to a nonequilibrium ionization (NEI) network in hydrodynamic simulations of radiative turbulent mixing layers. At $5<z<8$, they are at least 10 times more abundant than UV-selected quasars. Yet, how this population evolves towards lower redshift is unclear. Yet, how such systems thermalize far from equilibrium remains a fundamental open question at the crossroads of statistical, high-energy, and condensed-matter physics. items.authors: Sebastian Lahs, Thorsten Schumm, Victor V. Flambaum, David DeMille

items.authors: Yuuka Kanakubo, Volker Koch
items.abstract: Relativistic viscous hydrodynamics is a widely used theoretical framework for simulating quark-gluon plasma (QGP) dynamics in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. One open question is how to quantitatively assess the validity of a hydrodynamic description of such a system. In this work, we extract the poles of linear response functions from numerical simulations of hydrodynamics and Boltzmann transport. items.authors: S\'ebastien Rivat
items.abstract: This article traces the origins of Steven Weinberg's early conception of Effective Field Theories (EFTs) in the 1960s. I argue that Weinberg's path to his first EFT prototype was decisively shaped by his longstanding unificatory commitment. From his early days as a physicist onward, he strove to rely on first principles, whether fundamental or not, to bring order to the diversity of particle phenomena. items.title: Accretor Luminosity as Probe of Orbital Evolution and Magnetic Braking in AM CVn Binaries
items.authors: Tin Long Sunny Wong, Peter Scherbak, Jim Fuller
items.abstract: AM CVn binaries are ultracompact systems with orbital periods $P_{\rm orb} \lesssim 70$ min, where a white dwarf accretes from a He-rich semidegenerate donor. At short orbital periods ($P_{\rm orb} \lesssim 20$ min), rapid accretion reheats the accretor. As the system widens and the mass transfer rate decreases, the accretor follows standard white dwarf cooling at longer orbital periods ($P_{\rm orb} \gtrsim 30$ min). items.title: Calabi-Yau at 50: mathematical discovery in the age of AI
items.authors: Yang-Hui He
items.abstract: Using the golden jubilee of Yau's proof of the Calabi conjecture as a spring-board, we discuss how the dataset of Calabi-Yau manifolds brought together mathematicians and physicists since the 1980s, and then further brought in the world of machine-learning and AI since 2017. We give a historical account on the growth of the field of ``AI-assisted mathematics'' in the last decade, and comment on what culminated in 2026 as perhaps the most dramatic year in the history of mathematics since Euclid.

items.title: On a Supersymmetric Generalization of the Matytsin Formula
items.authors: Evgeny Porubov
items.abstract: We derive the leading asymptotics of the supersymmetric analogue of the Itzykson-Zuber integral for the supergroup $U(n|m)$ in the limit $n,m\to\infty$ when $n/m$ is kept finite. This generalizes the Matytsin result for $U(N)$. We show that it is described by the classical action of two independent Hamiltonian systems corresponding to the bosonic and fermionic sectors.

items.authors: Caio V. P. de Brito, Gabriel S. Denicol

items.authors: Xianguo Lu
items.abstract: In this conference contribution, I briefly review current experimental programmes measuring the Dirac CP phase {\delta}CP using accelerator neutrinos. I argue that the nuSTORM concept---neutrino beams from a muon storage ring---could provide high-quality electron-(anti)neutrino beams needed for the cross-section inputs to {\delta}CP measurements.

In this context, chromatic calorimetry is an emerging concept for electromagnetic calorimeters, with the potential to combine the precise energy measurement of homogeneous calorimeters with longitudinal reconstruction of particle showers. items.authors: Hisham Anwer, A. Adel, E. Omar
items.abstract: Neutron-star cores retain structural freedom beyond the constraints supplied by nuclear measurements. We quantify this freedom through an observable-dependent variance ceiling and identify radius--Love compensation as a mechanism suppressing nuclear constraints on tides. Across four data-conditioned equation-of-state families, a pulsar radius measured to 0.3 km paired with a binary tide measured to 10\% removes 44--68\% of the current logarithmic Love-number variance. The framework connects laboratory precision and complementary stellar measurements to core structure.
